episode.title: Prefer endpoint-specific credentials across OpenRouter resolution paths
episode.before: At parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, both the CLI's eager initialization path and the shared OpenRouter runtime resolver selected an explicit key first, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY. When both environment variables existed, an OpenRouter request could therefore receive the OpenAI credential and fail authentication.
episode.after: At merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a, both resolution paths select an explicit key first, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then OPENAI_API_KEY. The shared resolver retains OPENAI_API_KEY as a compatibility fallback when the endpoint-specific key is absent, and regression tests encode both the preferred-key and fallback branches.
episode.diff: The implementation swaps two environment-variable lookups in cli.py and hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py without changing explicit-key precedence or base-URL resolution. tests/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py adds two tests: one proving OPENROUTER_API_KEY wins when both variables are set and one proving OPENAI_API_KEY remains the fallback when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is absent. Overall first-parent diff: 3 files changed, 34 insertions, 2 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: Merge commit 221e4228ecb45daeda869471167c9823bd74196a has first parent dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2, merges PR #295, and states that it fixes issue #289 by resolving OPENROUTER_API_KEY before OPENAI_API_KEY in all code paths.

The implementation-side parent commit explains the failure: when both variables were set, the wrong key was sent to OpenRouter, causing authentication failures; it identifies cli.py and runtime_provider.py as the corrected paths.
Before the change, the CLI constructor initialized its API key as explicit api_key, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
evidence_units.source: git show dd9d3f89b9da7d62f61a0cbf7304f67faca367a2:cli.py, HermesCLI initialization near line 850

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, the shared OpenRouter runtime resolver selected explicit_api_key, then OPENAI_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then an empty string.
The CLI eager initialization path was changed to select explicit api_key, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then OPENAI_API_KEY.
The shared OpenRouter runtime resolver was changed to select explicit_api_key, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY, then OPENAI_API_KEY, preserving the empty-string terminal fallback.

HermesCLI._ensure_runtime_credentials calls the shared resolver with the requested provider and explicit credential inputs, rejects empty credentials, updates self.api_key and self.base_url, and invalidates an existing agent when credentials or routing change.
Agent initialization invokes _ensure_runtime_credentials before constructing AIAgent, and passes the resolved self.api_key and self.base_url into that client.
A regression test sets both credential variables, resolves an OpenRouter runtime, and asserts that the endpoint-specific OPENROUTER_API_KEY value is returned.
A fallback test removes OPENROUTER_API_KEY, leaves OPENAI_API_KEY set, resolves an OpenRouter runtime, and asserts that the generic OpenAI-compatible credential is returned.
The first-parent implementation diff changes only cli.py, hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py, and tests/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py, totaling 34 insertions and 2 deletions.

The checkout environment could not execute the focused test module because its Python interpreter does not have pytest installed; test behavior is therefore established from the committed regression oracles rather than a fresh passing run.

candidate_atomics.name: align-endpoint-credential-precedence
candidate_atomics.title: Align credential precedence with the selected endpoint
candidate_atomics.description: Reconcile every credential-resolution path so an explicitly supplied credential remains strongest, the credential dedicated to the selected endpoint wins over a generic compatible credential, and the generic credential remains a fallback.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent authentication failures caused by sending a credential for one service to a different selected endpoint when multiple compatible credential variables coexist.
semantic_action.module_role: Credential precedence policy shared by eager client state and runtime provider resolution
semantic_action.pre_state: The selected runtime is OpenRouter-compatible, no explicit credential overrides the environment, and both endpoint-specific and generic compatible credentials may be present; existing paths prioritize the generic credential inconsistently with the selected endpoint.
semantic_action.post_state: All inspected resolution paths use the invariant explicit credential > endpoint-specific credential > generic compatible fallback, so the selected endpoint receives its own credential when available.
semantic_action.validation: Compare the first-parent diff for both resolution paths and use the preferred-key regression test to prove the shared runtime resolver returns the endpoint-specific credential when both environment variables are populated.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-compatible-credential-fallback
candidate_atomics.title: Preserve the compatible credential fallback
candidate_atomics.description: Guard the precedence correction with an oracle proving that installations which only provide the generic OpenAI-compatible credential continue to resolve a usable key.

semantic_action.intent: Correct conflicting-credential selection without breaking configurations that rely on a generic compatible credential because no endpoint-specific credential is configured.
semantic_action.pre_state: The endpoint-specific credential is absent while a generic credential accepted by the selected compatible endpoint is present.
semantic_action.post_state: The resolver returns the generic compatible credential after exhausting the explicit and endpoint-specific slots.
semantic_action.validation: Run the fallback regression test with OPENROUTER_API_KEY removed and OPENAI_API_KEY set; it asserts the returned api_key equals the generic fallback value.

candidate_workflows.name: repair-conflicting-compatible-credential-resolution
candidate_workflows.title: Repair credential selection when compatible providers share environment variables
candidate_workflows.description: Establish endpoint-aware credential precedence across every path that can seed or refresh client authentication, then verify both the conflict case and the backward-compatible fallback case.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a selected endpoint receives its dedicated credential when multiple compatible credentials coexist, while retaining a documented fallback when the dedicated credential is unavailable.
when_to_use: Authentication fails only when credentials for multiple API-compatible services are simultaneously configured.
A runtime supports an endpoint-specific credential plus a generic compatible fallback.
Credential state can be initialized or refreshed through more than one code path.
anti_goals: Do not remove explicit caller-supplied credential precedence.
Do not change provider selection, base-URL selection, client protocol, or token-refresh behavior unless separate evidence requires it.
Do not delete the generic compatible fallback when existing configurations depend on it.
Do not log, compare by value in diagnostics, or expose secret credential contents.
not_applicable_when: The endpoint accepts only one credential source and no compatible fallback is supported.
The failure is caused by provider selection, base-URL routing, expired credentials, or token refresh rather than precedence.
The supposedly generic credential is not valid for the selected endpoint and therefore must be rejected instead of retained as a fallback.
inputs: inventory of eager and runtime credential-resolution paths
tests capable of isolating environment variables
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one path chooses a generic compatible credential before the selected endpoint's dedicated credential, allowing a valid dedicated credential to be shadowed when both exist.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every inspected path applies explicit > endpoint-specific > generic-compatible precedence; conflict and fallback regression oracles encode the contract; unrelated routing behavior remains unchanged.

steps.condition: Apply when the selected endpoint has a dedicated credential source and one or more resolution paths currently prefer a generic compatible source.
steps.validation: Inspect each changed resolution path and run the both-present regression case; the resolved credential must be the endpoint-specific value.

steps.condition: Apply when the generic credential is intentionally supported as a fallback for the selected endpoint.
steps.validation: Remove the endpoint-specific variable, retain the generic variable, and verify that runtime resolution returns the generic value.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: confirm every identified eager and runtime path has the same explicit > endpoint-specific > generic-compatible ordering.
Conflict regression: set both environment credentials and assert the endpoint-specific value wins.
Fallback regression: unset the endpoint-specific credential and assert the generic compatible value is still returned.
Call-site check: confirm resolved credentials are propagated to client construction or trigger client recreation when changed.
Focused test execution in a dependency-complete environment; this extraction could not perform that final rung because pytest is absent.
stop_conditions: Stop if the selected endpoint and accepted credential types cannot be established from implementation evidence.
Stop if another uninspected credential-resolution path can still shadow the endpoint-specific credential.
Stop and split the work if correcting precedence requires changing provider or endpoint routing semantics.
Do not claim dynamic validation complete until the focused regression tests run in an environment with pytest and project dependencies.
unresolved_or_deferred: A fresh focused test run is deferred because pytest is unavailable in the checkout environment.

Are there credential-resolution paths outside the two changed locations that were dynamically audited by the original authors? The commit states 'all code paths,' but the available direct evidence establishes the CLI eager path and the shared runtime resolver only.
